main_text.l: Tempestas, nec adhuc tristes hausère tenebræ,
Et caligo nocens, terræque immanis hiatus?
Non Erebi fratres, nondum te Tartara pœnis
Exercent scelerata, hominumq; Deïque flagellū?
Te super Omnipotens acrem nunquamne furorū
Terribilis pluet incumbens, penitúsque recidet?
Sed quid ego? non sic Deus omnia protinus igne
Corripit, aut sontes lacrymoso protinus orco
Plectit: sed iustum expectat (ne accersite) tēpus,
Quo scelus in cumulū crescat, molísque nefandæ
Incrementum ingens, ac se iam ferre laboret,
Et iam nutanti sub pondere sponte fatiscat,
Séque sui tandem penitus, penitúsque ruina
Obruat: scelerís scelus hauriat alta Vorago.
Vos igitur quos tanta tenet fiducia Vitæ
Et scelerum, rebus nunc indulgete caducis.
Ite: sed ista olim constabunt gaudia magno.
Mox aderit tempus, quū iam quas mente secatis
Spes interdiƈtas, inania Vota per auras
Discerpent Venti, fastúmque animosq; feroces
Molliet Vna dies, tandémque dolere docebit.

l.i: Ergo age Roma tuos, age fac pia Roma Cy- nados
Securos scelerum, satia te sanguine iusto
Dum licet, s nullū tibi fac iā crimen inasum:
Roma (Lupa nā cur author tuus Vbera frůstra

page.notes: Several words in the verse are doubtful, notably the long-s forms and the ligature-like marks in "fiducia Vitæ" and "Vota"; the Greek-style abbreviations and the hyphenated "Cy-nados" are as printed. "Vita" and "Vota" were read with capital V as printed.
